analysis:
Examined CI threat-review scanner test changes only; no provider, coordinator, attestation, encryption, cache or billing runtime code is in these units, so no canonical threat (TB-002/TB-003/TB-007/TB-009/TB-011, T-041, T-053 etc.) is directly affected.

.github/scripts/test-threat-budget.py:
- Head 664/671: the cross-file uncertainty test now expects [SONNET, SONNET] with no OPUS local rescan. It still asserts manual_review_reasons is set and clean() is false (head 674-676), so uncertainty still blocks merge clearance.
- Head 950-982 adds tests for three behaviors: a manual GitHub rerun hands off with no paid calls and no clearance; scanner runtime is bounded to 60-3000s with a 900s default and invalid values rejected; a Bedrock workload ceiling stops before integration without clearance. These tests strengthen fail-closed expectations.

.github/scripts/test-threat-diagnostics.py:
- Head 186-187 and 196 add plan_calls accounting assertions ([2, 1]) to the multi-tier integration test. Uncertainty propagation assertions are retained.

These are tests, not the scanner implementation. The implementation files (threat_review/budget_scan.py, budget_runner.py, bedrock.py, merge_policy.py) were not supplied. The next pass should therefore confirm two things in those files:
- Removing the OPUS depth pass on cross-file uncertainty still routes to human review rather than clearing.
- Rerun detection (GITHUB_RUN_ATTEMPT) cannot be spoofed to bypass review. Per the test, a rerun yields a non-clean report, which is fail-closed.

No security regression identified in the supplied evidence.
